eu_policy.title: 🇪🇺 European Union Policy
eu_policy.content:
• **EU AI Act (General Purpose AI Compliance):** Providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models with systemic risk must implement mandatory risk management systems and conduct adversarial testing. Previously: No binding transparency or safety testing requirements for base model providers. Now: Mandatory submission of detailed technical documentation and summaries of training data to the EU AI Office. Deadline: November 2026. Affected: All GPAI developers and deployers. Significant impact on tech-sector valuations and compliance costs for AI startups. [EUR-Lex]

• **Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) - Large Undertakings Phase:** Large non-listed companies meeting two of three criteria (>250 employees, >€50m turnover, or >€25m total assets) must publish audited sustainability reports according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS). Previously: Reporting was only mandatory for listed public-interest entities with over 500 employees. Now: Mandatory audited reporting for all large undertakings regardless of listing status. Deadline: Reporting for the 2025 financial year must be completed by early 2026, with finalized standards entering force this month. Affected: Medium-to-large Portuguese enterprises. High impact for Portuguese businesses scaling into the "Large" category. [European Commission]

• **EU Decision on Iberian Energy Interconnectors:** Mandatory 15% increase in electricity transmission capacity between Portugal and Spain to reduce the "energy island" effect. Previously: Capacity targets were non-binding recommendations based on the 2020 energy framework. Now: Binding capacity increase requirement with mandatory investment milestones to be met by year-end. Deadline: December 31, 2026. Affected: Transmission System Operators (TSOs) and energy infrastructure investors. Highly relevant for Portuguese energy utility portfolios and grid-tech investors. [EUR-Lex]

Why it matters: The shift from voluntary guidelines to binding technical and sustainability audits (AI Act and CSRD) significantly increases the operational overhead and liability for mid-to-large EU enterprises.

portugal_policy.title: 🇵🇹 Portugal Policy & Law
portugal_policy.content:
• **Decreto-Lei n.º 112/2026 (IRC Innovation Incentive):** Reduces the corporate tax rate for certified "Scale-up" companies. Previously: 17% on the first €50,000 of taxable income. Now: 12.5% on the first €100,000 of taxable income. This reduces the tax burden for growing tech companies and encourages capital reinvestment. Diário da República.

• **Lei n.º 45/2026 (Regional Investment Requirement):** Modifies the criteria for residency permits via investment funds. Previously: Minimum investment of €500,000 in any approved venture capital fund. Now: Minimum investment of €750,000, with a mandatory 60% allocation to funds investing in territories with low population density. This forces investment capital into rural areas rather than the Lisbon and Porto hubs. Diário da República.

• **Portaria n.º 3821/2026 (Salário Mínimo Nacional 2027):** Establishes the new national minimum wage entering into force on January 1, 2027. Previously: €820.00 per month. Now: €910.00 per month. Businesses must adjust payroll budgets for a 10.9% increase in base labor costs. Portugal.gov.pt.

• **Decreto-Lei n.º 98/2026 (Self-Employed Contribution Adjustment):** Adjusts the social security contribution base for independent workers (Recibos Verdes). Previously: Contributions calculated on 70% of the average quarterly income. Now: Contributions calculated on 60% of the average quarterly income. This increases the immediate net monthly income for freelance professionals. Diário da República.

Why it matters: The combination of lower corporate taxes for scale-ups and a significant minimum wage hike creates a polarized environment of high growth incentives for tech and rising operational costs for traditional SMEs.
